thread:
ashwin: Heads up — after landing the torch.compile + cudagraphs change on canary, seqlen=512 p99 jumped ~2x for a subset of workloads. Repro by switching runtime.autotune=true and using the new capture path.

maria: ugh. any logs or profile traces? did kernel selector flip to a different matmul kernel?

ashwin: attaching a short flame snippet I grabbed from perf-bot. Top shows a new kernel 'matmul_fused_fastpath_v2' taking most time vs previous 'matmul_tile32'. perf-bot: CPU summary pinned in thread.

perf-bot: 
```
PROFILE: session=run-2064
seqlen=512 batch=1 model=gptxx
prev_hot_kernels: [matmul_tile32, attn_win8]
current_hot_kernels: [matmul_fused_fastpath_v2, attn_win8]
p50_latency_ms: 12.3 -> 21.7
p99_latency_ms: 58 -> 118
```

devon: interesting — matmul_fused_fastpath_v2 expects static shapes w/ cudagraph capture. torch.compile seems to be emitting a graph variant that triggers that path when capture succeeds. for dynamic shape runs it sometimes falls back later which causes kernel churn.

maria: so it's capture-induced routing: the selector thinks the captured graph is better for seqlen512 but under our KV cache replay it ends up with micro-batching patterns that blow up due to different launch config.

ashwin: exactly. repro steps I used: toggle ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_HINT=1, set AUTOTUNE_PROFILE=1, run prime with seqlen=8 then send seqlen=512 requests in steady-state. Selector picks fused_fastpath because of the warmup profile.

jenni: can you paste the exact env toggles? I want to run on my TPU host (lol).

ashwin: ```bash
export ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_HINT=1
export AUTOTUNE_PROFILE=1
# runtime flags
--runtime.autotune=1 --runtime.kvcache=true
```

maria: quick mitigation: we can teach the selector to require a min_samples_per_shape threshold before switching kernel families, or clamp cudagraph-only kernels to only be valid when capture was done with the same batching pattern.

devon: another option — add a short-lived seqlen-bucketed sticky mapping: when seqlen changes drastically from warmup to steady-state, keep previous kernel until N requests confirm win. avoids flip-flop.

ashwin: both sound good. I sketched a patch that adds a "shape_stability" metric to autotuner and rejects families where stability<0.7. did basic unit tests — no regress locally.

maria: can you open an RFC PR with the perf numbers and the patch? include a small synthetic that reproduces the KV cache replay edge-case. we'll need canary gating.

ashwin: opened draft PR: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4123 — includes profiling traces and a test harness that simulates prime-with-short-seq then steady-long-seq.

perf-bot: Canary run (PR-4123) started: 10% traffic on canary-cluster-3. Will report qps/latency and kernel hist every 30m.

jenni: if we ship that, what's rollback plan if autotune blocks legit fastpath? can we have denylist by hw_arch + model_hash?

devon: yes — add an allowlist for architectures known to benefit from fused_fastpath_v2. Default behavior: stability gating + arch allowlist. If stability unknown, we bias to the safer older kernel.

maria: also add a metric we can alert on: kernel_flip_rate per route > 0.2 over 5m triggers auto-rollback of autotune-enabled policy.

ashwin: noted. I'll update PR with arch-allowlist and flip_rate alert rule. running extended canary now (perf-bot).

perf-bot: Canary update (30m): p99 for impacted route down to 62ms on PR-4123 canary vs 118ms on baseline – flip-rate observed 0.03, stability metric avg 0.82.

maria: great numbers. let's run 24h canary and then join on a quick ship/rollback decision tomorrow. thanks for fast triage. :pray: 

devon: one more thing — add a debug flag that forces selector to log the kernel_family and stability score on each decision (compact log line). put it behind runtime.debug.autotune=true. This will speed future sleuthing.

ashwin: added that to the draft. I'll also add a tiny note in the release notes about torch.compile + cudagraph interactions so oncall isn't surprised.

jenni: awesome. ping me when 24h finishes, I'll help with the rollout doc and QA. :thumbsup:

ashwin: will do — thanks team.
